item.title: #3594905: The run snapshot does not record the --as-user default caller
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +145/−16 · php +134/−14 · md +11/−2
  • Diff: 6d37449
  • Discussion: #3594905 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The run snapshot now records the default caller set with drush ai-eval:run --as-user, and Compare runs shows it as "Default caller". Previously a run as an anonymous visitor and a run as an administrator looked like they had identical settings. Runs recorded before this change count as having no default caller, so upgrading does not change comparisons with older runs. A re-grade keeps the caller of the run it re-grades.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EvalRunner adds default_caller_uid to the snapshot, cast to int when $targetConfig['default_caller_uid'] is set and NULL otherwise. RunComparability::compare() treats a missing key as NULL and, when the two values differ, adds a default_caller_uid entry to differences with a and b values. Per the added unit tests, differing callers produce a side_by_side result, and a legacy snapshot without the key compares as direct against one with NULL. ResultRegrader adds default_caller_uid to the list of snapshot keys carried over from the earlier run, and ResultsCompareController adds the "Default caller" label. No schema change.

The same commit also bundles fixes for #3594902, #3594903 and #3594904. In EvalOptimizeCommand, the failure filters (proposer prompt via formatFailures(), stored failure details, dry-run failure count) now include measured failures with a score of 0.0 and exclude questions with an error or unscored flag. In EnvelopeImporter, re-importing an envelope with the same evaluation_id now also compares target_id (source name plus dataset name) and reports a conflict if it differs, and the interval is read only from the pass rate item's score_details, so a quality score interval is no longer stored as a pass rate interval. Docs were updated accordingly.

item.title: #3594904: EEE import skips a changed dataset name as a duplicate
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +145/−16 · php +134/−14 · md +11/−2
  • Diff: 6d37449
  • Discussion: #3594904 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Re-importing an EEE envelope with the same evaluation_id but a different dataset name was reported as 'already imported' and skipped, leaving the stored row with the old test id. It is now refused as a conflict and nothing is written. An identical file is still skipped.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The imported test id (target_id) is built from source_name and source_data.dataset_name, but the measurement fingerprint omits source_data, so the fingerprint alone could not detect the change. In EnvelopeImporter, the row is now mapped with mapRow() before the duplicate lookup, and the lookup also selects target_id. A stored import is skipped only when both the fingerprint and target_id match the freshly computed row. Otherwise it is reported as conflict for evaluation_id ...: stored measurement or target differs. The fingerprint itself is unchanged and schema/*.schema.json is untouched. Tests cover a changed dataset conflicting without modifying the stored row, and an identical re-import still being skipped without a conflict. The import documentation now says a different measurement or target under the same evaluation_id is a conflict.

The same commit also bundles fixes tracked in #3594902, #3594903 and #3594905 (optimizer failure selection, default_caller_uid in run snapshots and comparability, interval handling in the importer), which are outside this issue.

item.title: #3594903: EEE import stores a quality-score interval as the pass-rate interval
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +145/−16 · php +134/−14 · md +11/−2
  • Diff: 6d37449
  • Discussion: #3594903 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Importing an EEE envelope that has no pass-rate metric no longer writes the quality score's confidence interval into the pass-rate interval columns. For example, a quality score of 4 with an interval of 3.8 to 4.2 used to be stored as pass_rate_ci_low = 3.8 and pass_rate_ci_high = 4.2. Now those columns stay empty unless the envelope reports a pass rate. Rows imported before the fix are not corrected by this change.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In EnvelopeImporter::mapRow(), the interval's score_details used to come from $passRateItem ?? $primary. It now comes only from $passRateItem['score_details'] ?? []. With no pass-rate result item there is no uncertainty data, so the CI low and high values stay null. The existing pass_rate_source provenance marker still separates "not reported" from a measured zero. No schema/*.schema.json change. A new kernel test in EnvelopeImporterTest imports a 0 to 5 quality metric with an interval of 3.8 to 4.2 and asserts pass_rate is 0.0 and both CI columns are null.

The same commit also carries fixes for sibling issues #3594902, #3594904 and #3594905, which the diff shows as follows: an importer conflict check that also compares target_id, EvalOptimizeCommand failure filtering that skips errored and unscored questions, and a recorded default_caller_uid that RunComparability compares.

item.title: #3594902: The optimizer drops failures that scored 0.0
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +145/−16 · php +134/−14 · md +11/−2
  • Diff: 6d37449
  • Discussion: #3594902 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval optimizer no longer ignores questions that failed with a measured score of 0.0. Before, a run where every failure scored 0.0 ended with "No failures to optimize". Failures are now selected the same way everywhere: the question did not pass, has no error, and is not unscored. Questions that errored or could not be scored are excluded.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EvalOptimizeCommand::formatFailures() skipped questions with avg_score === 0.0, meant to drop errored questions. It now skips a question only if it passed, has an error, or is flagged unscored. The stored failure details no longer filter on avg_score > 0 and use the same rule. The --dry-run failure count previously counted every non-passed question, errored ones included. It now uses the same rule.

The same commit also carries fixes for #3594903, #3594904 and #3594905: the run snapshot records default_caller_uid (from --as-user), and RunComparability treats a difference as side by side only (a missing value reads as no default caller). ResultRegrader carries default_caller_uid over to a re-grade. EnvelopeImporter now reports a conflict when the same evaluation_id arrives with a different target, and no longer reads the pass rate interval from a non pass rate item. Docs and tests were updated.

item.title: #3594901: A grader that cannot be loaded drops out of scoring without a sign
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +183/−55 · php +180/−54 · md +3/−1
  • Diff: c4da6db
  • Discussion: #3594901 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Before, if a grader could not be loaded (for example its module was uninstalled, or its plugin threw in its constructor), it was silently left out of scoring. Questions and gates could then pass without that grader's check, even if it was a must-pass grader. Now a run does not start when a grader cannot be loaded, and the error names the grader and the reason. A grader that is not installed gives Could not load grader "id": it is not installed. Re-grades (the admin UI and drush ai-eval:regrade) stop with the same message.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EvalRunner::createGraders() used to catch \Throwable, log it and drop the grader. It now still logs, then throws RunDatasetException::graderUnavailable(), a new factory on RunDatasetException (the class docblock is widened from dataset-only). That factory gives a short message for PluginNotFoundException and otherwise includes the plugin's own exception message.

For browser runs, doStartRun() checks graderManager->hasDefinition() for each configured grader before the run is created, so a missing grader means no run row and no active run. It checks only that the plugin exists, because graders are instantiated per step as the account that started the run. stepRun() now passes NULL graders to runQuestion()/runQuestionBody() (parameter type is now ?array), which load them lazily. If loading fails there, for example after the grader was removed mid-run, the question gets an error row with grader_scores empty, avg_score 0.0 and passed FALSE, and it counts toward the run's error_count. The repeated error-row arrays were extracted into questionError().

runTarget(), startRun() and regradeTarget() (via EvalRunnerInterface docblocks) can now throw RunDatasetException for this case. EvalRegradeCommand and RegradeForm catch it next to \InvalidArgumentException and show the message. No schema changes. The module docs were updated.

Upgrade

Code that calls EvalRunnerInterface::runTarget(), startRun() or regradeTarget() should also handle Drupal\ai_eval\Service\RunDatasetException, which it now throws when a grader cannot load:

catch (\InvalidArgumentException | RunDatasetException $e) {
  // Show $e->getMessage() as is.
}

Contribution

item.title: #3594900: The quality gate is checked on rounded values, so 199 of 200 passes a 100% gate
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +88/−39 · php +83/−36 · md +5/−3
  • Diff: e78191a
  • Discussion: #3594900 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval quality gate now compares the unrounded pass rate or average score with the threshold. Before, values were rounded to two decimals first, so 199 of 200 questions passing counted as 1.00 and cleared a 100% gate, and 159 of 200 (79.5%) cleared an 80% gate. Such runs now fail. The stored and displayed figures are still rounded to two decimals. Earlier runs that passed only because of rounding may have been marked as passing wrongly.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Scorer::scoreTarget() now gets its figures from a new public static Scorer::targetMetrics(). It returns valid_count, passed_count, avg_score and pass_rate, all unrounded, and skips errored and unscored questions as before. The gate goes through GateMetric::passesGate() with those values, and round(..., 2) is applied only to the returned avg_score and pass_rate.

Unrounded averages bring float error, so GateMetric::passesGate() now compares with a TOLERANCE of 1e-9. The code comment gives the example that three scores of 3.8 average to 3.7999999999999998 and must still meet a 3.8 gate. A new test covers this: 200 questions scoring 3.8 pass a 3.8 gate.

The repeated-run path in EvalOptimizeCommand::runRepeatedEval() had the same problem, because it averaged the already-rounded per-run pass_rate. It now calls Scorer::targetMetrics() on each result's question_scores, averages the unrounded values, and calls GateMetric::passesGate(). The private passesAggregatedGate() is removed. The docs were updated to describe the new behavior.

item.title: #3594899: The optimizer calls a score held out when most validation questions were used for training
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +59/−4 · php +53/−3 · md +6/−1
  • Diff: 2083bbc
  • Discussion: #3594899 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

When a dataset has split labels on only some questions and no splits block, unlabeled questions land in both train and validation. Previously the optimizer still reported the validation score as held out, with no warning. Now eval:optimize warns once per target, says how many validation questions were also used for training, and tells you to label every question or add a splits block. The baseline and final score lines also note the overlap.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The check lives in EvalOptimizeCommand::optimize(), in the dual-phase path (when a split protocol is active). With no splits block, it counts questions lacking a split key, which is the DatasetSplitter rule for unlabeled questions, and the splitter rule itself is unchanged. It counts questions rather than ids because a question may have no id. If the count is above zero, a warning goes to both $this->io()->warning() and $this->channelLogger->warning(), once per target.

The same count builds an $overlapNote such as (20 of 21 questions also in train). It is appended to the Baseline: line and to the Final score: line, which then reads on validation (...). A docblock that said "held-out validation" was reworded, and the optimizer docs were updated to describe the partial-label case. A new kernel test, testOverlappingValidationQuestions, covers two targets and checks each gets one warning.

item.title: #3594898: Applying a pending prompt candidate always fails
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +142/−2 · php +142/−2
  • Diff: 916b38a
  • Discussion: #3594898 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Clicking Apply on a pending prompt candidate on the AI Eval Optimize page used to always fail with an error, leaving the candidate pending and the agent prompt unchanged. Apply now saves the candidate prompt on the agent. If the agent has been deleted, Apply returns a "not found" response and the candidate stays pending.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

OptimizationController::apply() called $this->configFactory(), which ControllerBase does not provide, so the call threw and the transaction rolled back. The fix loads the ai_agent entity through entityTypeManager() and calls set('system_prompt', ...)->save() on it. Loading the entity rather than editing config directly means a deleted agent is not recreated as a config record holding only a prompt. If the ai_agents module is not installed, or the agent does not load, apply() throws NotFoundHttpException. The existing catch then rolls back the transaction, so the row stays pending. A new kernel test, OptimizationApplyTest, covers both the success path (row marked applied) and the deleted-agent path.

item.title: #3586790: Adopt Symfony AI Platform 0.12-0.14.1 changes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +516/−24 · php +508/−21 · yml +5 · json +3/−3
  • Diff: a3adad3
  • Discussion: #3586790 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

The AI module 2.x now works with Symfony AI Platform 0.14.1 instead of being pinned to 0.12. It also fixes streamed chat, which crashed with "Object of class ... could not be converted to string" whenever the model sent reasoning or tool call chunks. Models that reason before answering, such as NVIDIA ones, failed on every streamed chat. Streamed tool calls are now passed through to Drupal.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: symfony/ai-platform now requires ^0.14.1, symfony/ai-generic-platform ^0.14, and dev symfony/ai-gemini-platform ^0.14 (previously ^0.12).
  • New API: New Drupal\ai\Exception\AiStreamException (implements AiExceptionInterface); InputOutputConverter constructor takes an optional logger.

Technical details

InputOutputConverter::toStreamedChatOutput() used to cast every stream delta to string, which only works for TextDelta. The anonymous StreamedChatMessageIterator::doIterate() now maps deltas by type. TextDelta becomes a text chunk. ToolCallComplete becomes a chunk of OpenAI-shaped CreateStreamedResponseToolCall objects, one whole call each, which is the format the Drupal iterator reassembles tool calls from. Calls with an empty id (Gemini before 3.0) get a call_<index> id, and empty arguments are encoded as an empty JSON object. ToolCallStart, ToolInputDelta, the Thinking* deltas and MetadataDelta are skipped. Any other delta is skipped with a warning on the new logger.channel.ai channel, which is injected into ai.symfony.input_output_converter. A ChoiceDelta (multi-candidate stream) throws the new AiStreamException.

Tool schema building in the same class changed to match the 0.14 expectations. Each property now always carries a description and has its name key removed. The parameters array always includes required (possibly empty) and additionalProperties => FALSE. The Generic bridge now completes tool calls on any finish reason, which is why the stream fix matters more on 0.14. The issue lists follow-ups not covered here: no finish reason or token usage in streamed output, empty non-streamed token usage, Gemini text plus tool call losing the tool call, and the platform route ignoring ai.settings:request_timeout.

Upgrade

Update the Composer constraints. The requirements now resolve to:

"symfony/ai-platform": "^0.14.1",
"symfony/ai-generic-platform": "^0.14"

Run composer update drupal/ai --with-all-dependencies. Custom code that constructs InputOutputConverter directly can still do so, since the logger argument is optional.

item.title: #3586864: Translate the messages AI API Explorers write themselves for a failed run
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Version: 1.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +176/−41 · php +176/−41
  • Diff: 3b7e6c9
  • Discussion: #3586864 · 1 contributor · 16 comments

Summary

On a multilingual site, the AI API Explorers showed some failed-run messages in English even when the rest of the run card was translated, for example "The provider returned no audio." These messages the explorers write themselves are now passed through the translation system before they are stored and shown, so they can be translated like other interface text. English wording is unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Each explorer builds the message first, then throws it: $message = (string) $this->t('...'); throw new \RuntimeException($message);. The intermediate variable avoids the DrupalPractice "Exceptions should not be translated" phpcs warning. The run stores $exception->getMessage() as its error, so the stored error is in the language of the user who ran it. Covered: AiApiExplorerPluginBase ("Choose a provider and model."), Audio to Audio, Decision, Embeddings, Image Classification, Image to Image, Object Detection, Rerank, Text Classification, Text to Image, Text to Speech and ToolsExplorer (the "Access denied." fallback, the limits message, "You cannot run tools as this role."). Static methods (TextToSpeechGenerator::sample(), DecisionGenerator::parseQuestions()) use new TranslatableMarkup() instead of $this->t().

sprintf() messages became @placeholder strings. Because the exception message is plain text and escaped later when displayed, messages with placeholders are wrapped in Html::decodeEntities() so values such as a&b are not double-escaped (a DecisionGeneratorTest assertion covers this). Messages that were built from fragments became whole sentences: in EmbeddingsGenerator::toVector() the " for text N" suffix is now two separate strings per message, and in Text to Speech "Every voice failed." is translated and followed by the first error, which is already a translated sentence. The JSON parse error in parseQuestions() still comes from json_last_error_msg() and is not translated. The LogicException for developers is untouched. Tests testErrorIsTranslated were added for Audio to Audio and Tools, using locale_custom_strings_en overrides.

Upgrade

Custom explorer plugins that throw their own run errors can follow the same pattern:

// The run card shows this message to the user, so it is translated.
$message = (string) $this->t('The provider returned no audio.');
throw new \RuntimeException($message);

item.title: #3586870: Chat Explorer: add a "Render Markdown" checkbox under Output
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +455/−6 · php +408/−6 · css +26 · md +14 · yml +6 · txt +1
  • Diff: 6d65115
  • Discussion: #3586870 · 1 contributor · 22 comments

Summary

The Chat Explorer has a new Render Markdown checkbox on the Output tab. When it is on, assistant answers are shown as formatted HTML (headings, lists, code blocks, tables, strikethrough, and non-interactive task markers) instead of plain text. It is off by default and is saved with the chat. Copy, export and the history sent to the model keep the original raw text, and user, system and tool messages are displayed as before.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New markdown boolean in saved Chat Explorer chat settings (default FALSE), included in JSON export and import.

Technical details

The setting is added as markdown to ChatGenerator::SETTINGS and the defaults, handled like stream and structured as an unchecked-checkbox boolean, and validated as a bool on import. buildMessage() takes a new $markdown argument and, for assistant text without schema errors, calls the new markdownBlock() instead of textBlock(). markdownBlock() converts the text and passes the HTML through Xss::filterAdmin() before it is wrapped in a div with the aie-chat__answer--markdown class. When the option is on, the chat input also gets setHostnameFilter(new HostnameFilterDto(markdownMode: TRUE)).

The converter is a new ai_api_explorer.chat_markdown_converter service built by ChatMarkdownConverterFactory from ai.commonmark_converter_factory, so the shared ai.commonmark_converter is unchanged. The factory adds the table, strikethrough and task list extensions. The default task list renderer outputs <input> elements, which the XSS filter strips, so TaskListItemMarkerRenderer outputs a span with role="img" and an aria-label (Completed task or Incomplete task) containing a ☑ or ☐ character. New CSS in the explorer stylesheet covers .aie-chat__answer--markdown (normal whitespace, pre kept, table borders, horizontal overflow). The change also adds a README section, functional, FunctionalJavascript and kernel tests, including an XSS test and a streamed answer test.

item.title: #3586868: Chat Explorer: warn when Structured output is on but the schema is empty or not usable
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +105/−11 · php +105/−11
  • Diff: d231505
  • Discussion: #3586868 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

In the Chat Explorer, if Structured output is turned on but the JSON schema is empty, not valid JSON, or lacks a schema or properties key, the request is sent without a schema. The assistant's answer now shows a "Sent without a schema" notice, and the chat list only labels the chat "JSON schema" when a schema was really sent.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ChatGenerator::schema() returns NULL for unusable schemas. It now also rejects a full schema (with name/strict keys) whose inner schema is empty or not an array, instead of falling back to the wrapper as the schema. A new checkSchema() method replaces the duplicated validation in the non-streamed and streamed paths: with structured on and no schema it sets schema_missing on the answer message; otherwise it stores schema_errors from validateJsonSchema() as before. The streamed answer keeps the flag when the browser posts it back, via the answer-parsing code that copies schema_errors.

The message render adds a Sent without a schema notice when schema_missing is set. The chat list label now checks whether any message's meta.request.structured_output is set, instead of the structured input flag. ChatExplorerTest::testStructuredOutputWithoutSchema() covers empty, broken, keyless and empty inner schemas, plus the streamed path.

item.title: #3586708: Leading-zero item IDs in tool input skip Never include
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +595/−18 · php +564/−10 · md +31/−8
  • Diff: 1038ed5
  • Discussion: #3586708 · 1 contributor · 20 comments

Summary

Never include on a consumer now holds when the Get Relevant tool receives an item ID written with leading zeros, such as "0123" for item 123. Before, that spelling slipped past the exclusion and the item was delivered. The Load tool is also stricter: it accepts only integers and digit-only strings from 1 to 2147483647, so values such as 1e0, 1.0 or +1 no longer load an item, and the call reports No valid numeric context item IDs provided. when none are usable. Leading zeros and surrounding spaces are still accepted.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Never include on a consumer could be bypassed by passing an item ID with leading zeros (such as "0123") in always_include of the Get Relevant tool; fixed.

Technical details

The Never include subtraction in AiContextSelector::loadCandidateItems() used array_diff() on strings, so "0123" did not match "123", while the entity query compared the ID as a number and loaded item 123. The fix gives each numeric ID one spelling. AiContextNumeric (@internal) gets entityId(), which accepts integers and digit strings, trims whitespace and leading zeros, and rejects 0, floats, booleans and 1e0/1.0/+1. It has no upper limit, so Never include can still name an item with an ID above 2147483647 (possible on SQLite). boundedEntityId() applies the same rule and also rejects values above 2147483647 by comparing digit strings, without an integer cast.

AiContextItemIdentifierResolverTrait::resolveContextItemIdentifiersToIds() now uses entityId(), so both the always include and never include lists, from tool input or stored consumer config, normalize to the same string and duplicates collapse. An all-digit value that normalizes to nothing (0) is dropped and not treated as a UUID. AiContextLoadItemsFunctionCallBase::validateIds() uses boundedEntityId() instead of is_numeric(), since Load passes IDs straight to a query. As a defensive check, loadCandidateItems() also runs array_diff_key() to remove Never include items from the always-included group by loaded entity ID.

Unchanged behaviors: an explicit consumer_id in tool input still selects that consumer's config, always_include items skip hard-filter scopes, and the Load tool does not apply Never include. Docs gain an "Item ID format" section in docs/developers/function_calls.md.

item.title: #3583135: An optional map property's default value never reaches the tool
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +535/−22 · php +522/−19 · md +13/−3
  • Diff: 6ba8be7
  • Discussion: #3583135 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

When a caller sends a map input but leaves out an optional property that declares a default_value, the tool now receives that default. Previously the input schema advertised the default (for example "size": "medium"), but the tool saw an empty map. The same now holds for nested maps, maps inside lists, and maps keyed by name. Falsy defaults such as FALSE, 0 and '' are now advertised in the schema too.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

TypedInputsTrait::getExecutableValue() is restructured so every value source (locked, input, configuration, default) passes through a new private withPropertyDefaults() before prepareExecutableValue() and validation. The method walks MapDataDefinition properties, ListDataDefinition items, and the item values of a MapInputDefinition that has an item definition. It fills a property only if it is absent, optional, and has a non-NULL default, and it recurses into the filled default.

Required properties are not filled, so a missing required property is still reported by validation. An absent optional map still stays NULL, and a property sent as null stays null. The issue says that case waits on #3583106.

In InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer, the schema default check changes from truthiness to !== NULL, so FALSE, 0 and '' defaults are advertised. To stop a multiple definition's empty-list default from now appearing on each item, the cloned item definition gets setDefaultValue(NULL). This also removes the earlier documented difference where a default value was no longer advertised on each item. SchemaSampleGeneratorTrait now builds a sample for a keyed map from its additionalProperties item schema. The diff adds the map_property_default_tool test tool, and a kernel test, MapPropertyDefaultTest, covers it.

  • Changes: 6 files, +60/−18 · css +60/−18

Summary

Text in the AI API Explorers is easier to read. In Gin dark mode the muted text (run chips, segmented controls, view switches, task descriptions) was 4.21:1 against its background, below the 4.5:1 WCAG 2.2 asks for. It is now lighter. Status pills, hub filter counts, the Embeddings similarity matrix, and the faded rows in Rerank and the threshold bars were also changed so their text reaches the required contrast in light and dark mode.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: AI API Explorer CSS tokens changed: --aie-muted is lighter in Gin dark, --aie-primary-text is now a mix, and new --aie-danger-text and --aie-green-text tokens exist; custom themes overriding these may need review.

Technical details

The main fix is in css/explorer-ui.css. Inside .gin--dark-mode .aie, --aie-muted is now color-mix(in srgb, var(--gin-color-text-light, #545560) 75%, var(--aie-text)). It is built from Gin's token rather than from itself, which would loop. --aie-muted-strong is mixed from it, so it gets lighter too. Gin light is not touched.

Coloured text now uses new tokens mixed towards --aie-title: --aie-primary-text (65% of the Gin primary), --aie-danger-text, --aie-green-text, and a stronger --aie-warning-text (45% instead of 60%). They are used by .aie-status--ok and .aie-status--error, .aie-tools__req, .aie-tools__arg and .aie-rerank__row--up .aie-rerank__move. The pressed .aie-hub__filter .aie-count swaps its colours (primary text on an --aie-on-primary background). .aie-btn--primary:active is listed so Gin's a:active colour does not override the button text. Selected file, task and size cards switch their secondary text to --aie-muted-strong on the tinted selection.

Faded rows no longer use opacity on text. .aie-bar--dim and .aie-rerank__row--below now fade only the bar fill (.aie-bar__fill, .aie-rerank__fill), and the label, text and value keep --aie-muted. In embeddings.css the matrix heat is capped at 35% of the accent (calc(var(--aie-heat, 6%) * 0.35)), so the title colour stays readable. .aie-embeddings__hi no longer switches to --aie-on-primary and is only bolder, and the legend gradient was adjusted to match.

item.title: #3594897: Explain metrics and terms on the admin pages, with a link to the glossary
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 39 files, +1091/−93 · php +894/−77 · md +105/−9 · css +47 · js +33 · yml +10 · txt +2 · neon +0/−7
  • Diff: cece135
  • Discussion: #3594897 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval's admin pages now explain their own jargon. Terms such as Overall error, Average gap, TPR, TNR, n, Split, Config version, Gate, Unscored, Corrected pass rate, Trend, Taxonomy, EEE and OTLP get a small "?" button. Clicking, tapping or pressing Enter on it opens a short definition with a "Learn more" link to the matching glossary entry on the docs site. Escape or a second click closes it. The calibration, judges, results, compare, traces, failure mode and import pages also get a short help text with a link to the relevant user guide. The glossary gained entries for the terms that had none.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Labels and headers on AI Eval admin pages now include a .ai-eval-toggletip button and popover bubble, which can change exact-text selectors.
  • New API: New ai_eval_toggletip render element with Toggletip::term() and Toggletip::cell() helpers, the ai_eval/toggletip library and generated GlossaryTerms::all() definitions.

Technical details

The definitions come from one source, docs/user/glossary.md. scripts/glossary-to-php.php parses the first paragraph of each entry with GlossaryMarkdown::parse() and writes src/Help/GlossaryTerms.php, a generated class of TranslatableMarkup strings keyed by glossary anchor, so the definitions can be extracted for translation. After editing a first paragraph you must rerun the script. A unit test (GlossaryTermsTest) compares the generated class with the glossary. The README documents the workflow.

The UI is a new render element, #type => 'ai_eval_toggletip' (Drupal\ai_eval\Element\Toggletip), with #term (the glossary anchor) and #label. Two static helpers wrap it: Toggletip::term($term, $label) for any render array, and Toggletip::cell($term, $label) for a table header or body cell. It renders the label, a <button popovertarget> and a <span popover> bubble using the native popover attribute, with no Ajax. The new ai_eval/toggletip library (css/toggletip.css, js/toggletip.js, depending on core/drupal and core/once) is attached only when a known term renders. The JS only positions the bubble near its button on toggle. An unknown anchor logs a warning once and falls back to the plain escaped label.

Placements cover the calibration list and detail pages, the judges table and validation history/compare, results list, detail and compare, failure rate table, failure mode list, trace review verdict filter and the two import forms. Some explanatory prose on those pages was removed in favor of the popovers, for example the TPR/TNR hover title text and the overall-error sentence on the callers form. Because a label cell now also contains the button and the definition text, existing tests that matched exact cell text were changed to starts-with(...) XPaths or strip the toggletip nodes. A new HelpHooks class implements hook_help for these routes and links to the guide pages. The glossary and the failure rate and average score definitions were also reworded. GraderPluginManager now names the deprecated annotation class as a string, and a phpstan baseline entry for it was removed.

Upgrade

Only relevant if you render your own admin tables or tests against AI Eval pages. To add a definition to a label, use the glossary anchor:

use Drupal\ai_eval\Element\Toggletip;

$header[] = Toggletip::cell('overall-error', $this->t('Overall error'));

Tests that match the exact text of an AI Eval label or header may need starts-with(normalize-space(.), "..."), since the cell now also contains the "?" button and its definition.

item.title: #3586862: Lay out right-to-left text in AI API Explorer results in its own direction
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 16 files, +555/−19 · php +477/−18 · css +57 · md +21/−1
  • Diff: 719624f
  • Discussion: #3586862 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

Right-to-left text (Arabic, Hebrew, Farsi, Urdu) in AI API Explorer results, such as run titles, quotes, outputs, chat bubbles and transcripts, was laid out left to right, so it started at the left edge and its punctuation landed next to the first word. These blocks now take their direction from the text, so right-to-left text is right-aligned with punctuation at its end. English and other left-to-right text looks as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: ExplorerUi::isolate() and ExplorerUi::languageDirection() added for explorer plugins that show free text or mixed labels.

Technical details

css/explorer-ui.css gets one rule with unicode-bidi: plaintext and text-align: start for the shared classes (.aie-run__title, .aie-quote, .aie-output) and for the explorer-specific blocks that hold free text (chat, extractive QA, rerank, speech to text, speech to speech, moderation, tools, object detection labels and others). plaintext takes each paragraph's direction from its first strong character. A second rule, .aie [dir] { unicode-bidi: isolate; }, keeps an explicit dir working, because plaintext would ignore it.

Two helpers are added to ExplorerUi. languageDirection(string $code) returns rtl or ltr from LanguageManager::getStandardLanguageList(), or NULL for an unknown code. isolate(string $text) wraps text in U+2068 and U+2069, which works like <bdi> but is also usable in attributes and <option> labels. The Translate explorer uses languageDirection() to set dir on the output from the target language and on the quote when the source language was picked, not detected, which fixes an Arabic translation that starts with a Latin word. Speech to Speech sets dir and lang on its texts. Embeddings labels ("T2 · text") use isolate(). The Speech to Speech and Text Classification run titles wrap file names and labels in <bdi>, and ObjectDetectionGenerator gives the label cell the aie-object-detection__label class. The module README gains a "Showing text in any language" section, and new Functional and FunctionalJavascript tests cover the behavior.

Upgrade

For custom explorer plugins that show user or model text: put the text in a block with aie-run__title, aie-quote or aie-output, or add your own class to the rule in css/explorer-ui.css. Where the language is known, set dir from ExplorerUi::languageDirection(). For a label that puts a prefix before a text, use <bdi> or ExplorerUi::isolate():

'label' => $label . ' · ' . ExplorerUi::isolate($names[$j]),

item.title: #3586403: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Chat Generation Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 23 files, +6543/−1477 · php +3875/−778 · css +1570/−503 · js +1032/−139 · md +34/−44 · twig +26 · yml +6/−13
  • Diff: 15068d5
  • Discussion: #3586403 · 1 contributor · 30 comments

Summary

The Chat Explorer has been redesigned on the shared explorer layout. It now supports a full message history instead of a single message, with system, user, assistant and tool roles. Several chats can be kept and reopened when run history is on. Tool calls and their results are shown in the thread, and the model can be set to only show a call, run it, or run it and continue for up to 5 rounds. Request settings (model, tools, output, code) sit in tabs, chats can be imported and exported as JSON, and structured output answers are checked against the schema. Provider and model selection now use the ai_provider_configuration element. The generated code example no longer contains the broken calls and unescaped values it had before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers, front-end developers and site owners.

  • Security: AiValidator no longer fetches external documents referenced by $ref in a user-supplied JSON schema; it returns a validation error instead.
  • Theme change: Chat Explorer renders through the new ai-api-explorer-chat.html.twig template; the ai_api_explorer/stream and ai_api_explorer/multiselect libraries are removed.
  • New API: ExplorerRunManager::getRuns() takes a new $sort argument (created or changed); new ai_api_explorer_chat theme hook and explorer.chat library.

Technical details

ChatGenerator was rewritten around a stored chat (an ExplorerRunInterface run) holding messages and settings (provider, tools, tool_mode, stream, structured, schema, guardrail_set). It is saved after every turn through ExplorerRunManager; with history off the chat lives in form state and the chats column only lists the open chat. Layout comes from a new ai_api_explorer_chat theme hook (template_preprocess_ai_api_explorer_chat() splits the form into chats, thread, settings and import), the explorer.chat library (css/explorers/chat.css, js/explorers/chat.js), and MAX_ROUNDS = 5 caps automatic tool rounds. Streaming is done in the new chat script, so the old stream.js, stream.css, multiselect.js and the multiple-select assets and their libraries are deleted.

ExplorerRunManager::getRuns() gains a $sort parameter (created default, or changed), and the purge of runs past the count limit now orders by changed, so a chat that is still used is kept over a newer but idle one.

The code example is built with \Drupal::service(...), passes the normalized tool definitions to new ToolsInput($functions), and escapes message text and schema values. Outside the explorer, AiValidator::validateSchema() now uses a UriRetriever backed by an empty PredefinedArray, so schema references inside the document resolve but a $ref to a URL or file is never fetched; it returns "The schema references an external document, which is not supported." The mdxeditor build also gets safeHtmlNodes so HTML in the markdown shows without scripts or event handlers (requires rebuilding the editor assets).
